advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a manifest_file_scope case asserting a manifest with multiple 'file-scope:' lines (e.g. duplicate 'file-scope: none', or 'file-scope: none' plus another value) returns 'unscoped'.
evidence: tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py:366-369 parametrization covers only single 'file-scope: none', single 'file-scope: future-scope', and None — no multi-line case

ABSENCE: search for `file-scope:` in tests/ returns only single-line cases (test_attestation_invalidation.py:367,369,379,445; test_plan_review.py:790); no test constructs a manifest with two file-scope lines to assert the strict-equality fail-closed result
advisory.finding: manifest_file_scope's strict list-equality guard (declarations == [_FILE_SCOPE_NONE]) that fails closed to 'unscoped' when a manifest carries MORE THAN ONE 'file-scope:' line is untested; tests only cover a single 'file-scope: none', a single unknown value ('file-scope: future-scope'), and an absent line. A regression relaxing the guard to a membership/any check (which would classify a manifest containing a duplicate or extra 'file-scope:' line as 'none' and wrongly skip whole-HEAD drift) would not be caught.
scenarios: A signer or migration emits both a legacy and a new 'file-scope:' line, or a duplicate 'file-scope: none'; the exact-list guard must still return 'unscoped'.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_manifest_file_scope_contract_preserves_legacy_bytes (or the classifier table), assert `attest.manifest_file_scope([*legacy, 'file-scope: none', 'file-scope: none']) == 'unscoped'` and `attest.manifest_file_scope([*legacy, 'file-scope: none', 'file-scope: other']) == 'unscoped'`.
